messages:
Alex (customer): Hey - we keep getting 429s from the API during a nightly ingest window. We're on the free tier and thought there was some burst allowance. Error is 'rate_limit_exceeded' and the client shows Retry-After: 30. Is this expected? We're blocked for a couple hours and it's failing downstream jobs.
Maya (Support): Sorry you're hitting this, Alex. Can you paste the exact error body and the x-rw-* headers if present? Also which endpoint (completions/embeddings) and approximate token rate during the spike?
Alex (customer): embeddings endpoint. We send ~800 concurrent small requests (64 tokens each) during the shard run. Error body: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"token quota exhausted"} Headers: x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0, Retry-After: 30, x-rw-plan: free-0.
Maya (Support): Got it. On free tier the burst window is small and sustained concurrency like that will exhaust token quota quickly. Two quick mitigation ideas: 1) add exponential backoff + jitter on 429s, 2) smooth the requests to lower concurrency (throttle to ~100 concurrent) while you evaluate upgrade. Can you share a minimal repro curl/snippet?
Alex (customer): repro (node):
```js
// simplified
const p = []
for (let i=0;i<800;i++) p.push(fetch('/v1/embeddings',{method:'POST',body:...}));
await Promise.all(p);
```
This is what the job looks like. We don't want to slow it too much because we're on a tight SLA for indexing.
Rajat (Support-Eng): That pattern will spike concurrent connections and exhaust free-tier tokens fast. For embeddings the platform counts per-embedding cost (tokens * per-embedding unit). Short term: add a concurrency limiter (bottleneck libs or a simple queue) and retry logic: exponential backoff starting at 250ms with max cap ~8s and jitter. Also watch for the Retry-After header — it's authoritative.
Maya (Support): Also you can confirm token usage on your account via the usage endpoint in the console — that will show the minute-by-minute burn. If you want a quick temporary lift, we can request a short-lived burst from Billing while you migrate to a paid plan. Sam from Billing can advise on what's possible.
Sam (Billing): Hi all — we can do a one-off temporary increase for accounts with clear reasons. We'll need: account id, owner email, approximate sustained tokens/hour, and preferred start/end window. Note: free tier exceptions are granted sparingly; usually we recommend moving to a paid tier if this pattern repeats.
Alex (customer): Account id: acct_01G9EXAMPLE. Owner: alex@example.com. Peak tokens during window ~1.5M tokens over 30m (embeddings counts applied). We can provide logs. Can you estimate cost for moving to paid?
Priya (Sales): Hey Alex — thanks. For steady ingestion at that scale you have two options: 1) pay-as-you-go (hosted) — straightforward, per-embedding unit pricing, no long-term commitment, or 2) Dedicated/Reserved capacity — if you need deterministic throughput and lower per-token cost. Ballpark: with pay-as-you-go you'd see roughly X$/M tokens (I gave a rough number in DM; want to avoid noise here). If you want a formal quote or reserved capacity, I can spin up pricing and SLA options.
Alex (customer): We need the short-term burst today and then a path to paid. Can Support/Billing coordinate?
Maya (Support): I'll file an internal ticket for the temporary spike. Sam, can you approve a short 24-48h temporary uplift to avoid job failures while Sales and the customer decide?
Sam (Billing): I can approve a 24h uplift to cover the ingest window. I need confirmation of the expected token cap and that the account owner approves charges if we move beyond the trial uplift. Please reply in-thread with the acceptance.
Alex (customer): Confirmed — account owner approves charges if we exceed uplift and move to paid. Please set uplift to cover up to 2M tokens over the 24h window.
Rajat (Support-Eng): For reproducibility and to help you long term, here's a sample retry snippet (python):
```python
import time, random
for attempt in range(6):
    res = call_api()
    if res.status_code == 429:
        ra = int(res.headers.get('Retry-After', 1))
        sleep = min(8, (2 ** attempt) * 0.25) + random.uniform(0, 0.1)
        time.sleep(max(sleep, ra))
        continue
    break
```
And for concurrency throttling consider a simple semaphore with concurrent limit = 100-200 during the job.
Maya (Support): I'll also add a note to the ticket recommending the customer uses per-route caching (if many repeated inputs) and batching where possible — both reduce token burn.
Priya (Sales): Alex, I'll prepare options and a quick quote (payg vs reserved) and ping you in DM. If you want a sales-assisted increase (multi-month committed), we'll fast-track a contract and reserved capacity onboarding — there is a short technical review for Dedicated.
SupportBot: Ticket created: #SUP-2025-892 (temporary uplift request). Assigned: Billing + Support-Eng.
Sam (Billing): Uplift scheduled. I've provisionally added +2M token headroom for the next 24 hours. Monitor and report if you still see 429s.
Alex (customer): Thanks — I'm rerunning the job now with the semaphore and backoff in place. Will report back in ~1h. Really appreciate the quick help. :pray:
Maya (Support): Glad it helped. If you still see errors after the uplift, please paste the exact headers and we'll escalate to Eng-SRE. If you decide to migrate to paid, Priya will handle the handoff.
Alex (customer): Update: job completed successfully with the adjustments. No 429s after the uplift. Will follow up about pricing tomorrow. 
Rajat (Support-Eng): Good to hear. Filing a small playbook entry for support: guidance on free-tier burst behavior, suggested concurrency limits for embeddings, and example retry code. Will link to the ticket.
Maya (Support): Closing loop here — ticket will remain open until billing confirms final charge policy. Alex, feel free to reopen if anything else crops up. :thumbsup:
